Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’m here to help you settle into new-motherhood by checking on your emotional well-being. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the **EPDS**—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—which looks at mood, anxiety, and self-harm thoughts in the past week. Everything you share stays between us unless safety is a concern, and we’ll go at your pace. There are just ten questions; I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer however feels easiest. Ready to start?

1. Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt hard to do?
I’ve still been able to laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes silly faces at the baby—but I’ve noticed I don’t find things quite as amusing as I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, yeah. My husband will do something goofy with the baby and I’ll laugh, but it feels kind of forced—like I’m going through the motions. Most of the time I just feel too tired or pre-occupied to really find things funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like my morning coffee or when my mom comes over to hold the baby so I can shower—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. Even outings feel more like chores I have to check off than something I genuinely anticipate.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I kept thinking it must’ve been something I ate that upset her through the milk. My partner said she’s just being a baby, but I still felt like I’d done something wrong. It’s not every minute—just little moments where I think, “If I were better at this, she wouldn’t cry so much.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly feel this knot in my stomach, like something bad’s about to happen, even if everything’s quiet. I’ll check the baby’s breathing three or four times a night, worried something’s wrong even though she’s fine. I can usually talk myself down, but the worry pops up out of nowhere a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

It’s only happened once or twice this week—like yesterday when I was folding laundry and suddenly my heart started racing and I felt shaky for no reason. It passed after a minute, but it left me kind of rattled.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… a couple of days this week it’s felt like the sink is piled with bottles, the laundry’s multiplying, and no matter how much I cross off, the list just grows. I’ll be rocking the baby and think, “I can’t keep up,” but then I take a breath and chip away at it. I’m managing, just sometimes feels like I’m one step away from dropping everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve been tired enough that I usually fall asleep pretty fast once the baby settles. Sometimes I’ll lie there running through what I didn’t get done, but I still drift off within maybe 20 minutes.
I have felt sad or miserable

I’ve had moments—like when the baby won’t nap and I’m stuck on the couch—where I just feel this heaviness and my eyes tear up. It’s not all day, maybe a little wave in the afternoon or right before my partner gets home, but it’s there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried twice this week. Once was when she wouldn’t latch and I felt like I was failing at the one thing I’m supposed to be able to do for her. The other time was just yesterday—everything was actually quiet, but I suddenly felt overwhelmed and the tears came for a minute or two.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt tired and weepy, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary**  
*Patient*: Postpartum mother, ≤12 wks post-delivery (per chart)  
*Date*:

**A. Self-reported symptoms**  
- **Affective**: Intermittent sadness, “heaviness,” tearfulness 2× this week; enjoyment markedly diminished (coffee, shower breaks only “look-forward” items).  
- **Cognitive**: Unwarranted self-blame (infant crying) & “can’t keep up” thoughts; racing-heart panic episodes 1-2×/wk, anticipatory worry 2-3×/day, nocturnal safety-checking.  
- **Behavioral**: Crying spells, forced laughter, chores feel obligatory.  
- **Physical**: Fatigue, 1-min shakiness/racing heart; sleep onset ≤20 min once infant settled.

**B. Positive screens**  
- EPDS items consistent with possible minor-moderate depression (items 8, 9) and anxiety (items 4, 5).  
- No self-harm ideation (item 10 denied).

**C. Pattern**  
- Symptoms fluctuate, worse late afternoon/evening; coping remains partially intact (self-soothing, partner support).  
- No psychotic features, obsessional thoughts of harm to infant, or suicidal intent.

**D. Risk factors noted**  
- Primiparous, sleep fragmentation, high self-expectations, absence of prior mental-health treatment reported.

**E. Screening conclusion**  
Elevated depressive & anxiety symptoms above “baby blues” threshold; warrants formal EPDS scoring, further clinical evaluation for minor-moderate postpartum depression and/or anxiety, psychoeducation, and safety-planning; immediate safety risk appears low (no self-harm ideation).
